source_mainboard_cards: Kumano Faces Kakkazan // Etching of Kumano

conclusion.summary: The low-curve mono-red shell, burn, pump and sideboard interaction transfer well. The current Pioneer role-compression package and creature-land resilience do not.

direct_transfers.notes: Best direct transfer of the Pioneer one-drop engine.

direct_transfers.card: Kumano Faces Kakkazan // Etching of Kumano
direct_transfers.notes: Legal and strategically relevant, but the creature body is not available immediately.
Direct flexible burn; four damage requires kicker and must not be assumed on curve.
Direct pump transfer, but it requires a creature and exposes the deck to removal in response.
Direct legal interaction, but requires a legal own-creature target and cannot damage the opponent.
Direct legal reach land; the damage is neither free nor early.
Directly legal, but only supports Lizard, Mouse, Otter or Raccoon creatures. Its value depends on the final creature types.

functional_replacements.notes: Sawblade Scamp is one mana but converts spell casts into oil and requires tapping; the two-mana alternatives preserve spell scaling but not curve compression.
Pump/trample and reload exist, but not on one efficient creature.
The pool can prevent lifegain, but cannot reproduce the complete pressure and resilience package.
Anti-lifegain is available; the immediate top-end damage package is not.
Interaction is plentiful, but a separate threat slot is required.

functional_replacements.missing_original: Mutavault / Den of the Bugbear / Sokenzan, Crucible of Defiance
functional_replacements.notes: Reach and land/spell flexibility exist, but not the same resilient board pressure. MDFCs enter tapped on the land side.

non_reproducible_functions: A twelve-slot one-mana engine cannot be copied with three names at four copies; the Thun three-copy rule requires at least four distinct one-mana cards and lowers average card quality.
No checked common or uncommon reproduces Screaming Nemesis or Sunspine Lynx role compression.
No checked common or uncommon reproduces Bonecrusher Giant as both interaction and a threat from one card.
The checked pool has no direct equivalent to Mutavault or Den of the Bugbear as resilient creature-land pressure.
Persistent anti-lifegain exists only on narrower or slower cards and cannot be counted as immediate damage.

one_mana_or_turn_one: Kumano Faces Kakkazan // Etching of Kumano

open_questions: Can four distinct one-mana packages reach acceptable opening-hand quality under the three-copy rule?
Is the loss of rare midgame role compression better answered by a lower, faster curve or by adding explicit reload slots?
Does Rockface Village have enough legal creature-type targets in the best generated shell to justify colorless early mana?
Can Ramunap Ruins provide enough late reach without overloading the mana base with colorless sources?
